sections.overview: Pallas’s sandgrouse is an Asian sandgrouse of open, dry country, with a range centred on Central Asia.
sections.identification: It is a slender, pigeon-sized bird with sandy, dark-speckled plumage, a black belly and a long pointed tail.
sections.habitat: It favours sparsely vegetated semi-deserts, deserts and dry steppe on varied open soils.
sections.diet: Seeds form the main part of its diet; it also takes plant shoots, leaves and flowers, with insects reported only rarely.
sections.behavior: It is a mobile species that can erupt beyond its usual range, sometimes reaching western and northern Europe.
sections.reproduction: It nests on the ground; the Russian species account describes a typical clutch of three eggs.
sections.ecology: Access to waterholes is important in its dry habitats, and flocks regularly visit them to drink.
sections.conservation: A Russian regional account reports declines in parts of Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan, but those local notes do not establish a global trend.
